draft.title: Network terms
card: Vertex
a point in a network, drawn as a dot. It can stand for a town, a computer or a person.
Edge
a line that joins two vertices. It can stand for a road, a cable or a friendship.
Degree
the number of edges that meet at a vertex. If town A has roads to B, C and D, then A has degree 3.
Weighted network
a network with a value on each edge, such as a distance in km or a cost in dollars. The value is called the weight.
draft.remember: A network is vertices joined by edges. Degree counts edges at a vertex, and weights are values on edges.

a.q: In a network, vertex P is joined by edges to Q, R, S and T. What is the degree of P?
a.why: Degree is the number of edges that meet at the vertex. P has four edges, one to each of Q, R, S and T, so its degree is 4. The answer is not 5, because P itself is not counted as one of its own edges.
a.clue: Count the edges at P, not the vertices in the network.

b.q: A network shows five towns as dots. Roads between them are lines labelled 12, 7, 9 and 15, in km. What do the labels 12, 7, 9 and 15 show?
b.why: A value written on an edge, such as a distance, is its weight. The labels are on the roads, which are edges, so they are not degrees. Degree is a count of edges at a vertex, and it is not a distance.
b.clue: The labels sit on the lines, not on the dots.

problems.detail: The why says 'P itself is not counted as one of its own edges', which blurs vertices and edges. Better: 'The answer is not 5, because degree counts edges at P, not the vertices P, Q, R, S and T.'
